items.claim: Novo Nordisk oplyste, at selskabet i ugen forinden fortsatte tilbagekøb af egne B-aktier under det aktietilbagekøbsprogram, der blev indledt 4. februar 2026.

JPMorgan-analytiker Richard Wotser fastholdt en neutral vurdering og henviste til begrænset effekt af generisk konkurrence samt stærkere end ventet international vækst for Wegovy, mens han samtidig sænkede sine forventninger til den orale Wegovy-version.

Deutsche Bank nedgraderede Novo Nordisk til 'sælg', og analytiker Emmanuel Papadakis sagde, at banken har sænket sine estimater for omsætningen på mellemlangt sigt efter de skuffende resultater fra Ziltivekimab-studiet.
items.source: Emmanuel Papadakis, Deutsche Bank (refereret af Invezz)

items.claim: Deutsche Bank anførte desuden som begrundelse, at der er usikkerhed om, hvorvidt selskabet kan vende tilbage til meningsfuld vækst i 2027, og at en udvidet Medicare-dækning af vægttabsmedicin i USA kun ventes at give begrænset salgsløft.

Novo Nordisk oplyste, at tilbagekøbet af egne B-aktier fortsatte under det delprogram, selskabet indledte 6. maj 2026 som del af det samlede program vedtaget for en 12-måneders periode fra 4. februar 2026.

Q2 2026 and H1 2026: Adjusted net sales for Q2 2026 reached DKK 78,488 million (7% growth at CER), beating analyst consensus. Adjusted operating profit was DKK 33,389 million (up 11% at CER), and adjusted diluted EPS was DKK 6.18, beating expectations. However, reported operating profit declined 16% due to DKK 6.3 billion in non-cash pipeline impairment charges.
Q2 2026 / H1 2026: It updates our understanding of revenue growth, margin compression, and guidance for the remainder of 2026 following the 2025 Annual Report.
U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington: Jury found Novo Nordisk not liable in a whistleblower False Claims Act litigation regarding off-label promotion of NovoSeven.
PMCPA (UK): Fined and publicly reprimanded for failing to properly disclose £1.24 million in transfers of value to healthcare and patient organizations.
Office of the Minnesota Attorney General: Settled deceptive insulin pricing enforcement by agreeing to cap out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35 per month for five years.
PMCPA (UK): Public reprimand for voluntary disclosure of systemic failures to report approximately £7.8 million in transfers of value between 2020 and 2022.
FTC / FDA: Challenged 17 delivery-device patents listed in the Orange Book for Ozempic, Saxenda, and Victoza.
U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania: Consolidated consumer-harm and product liability litigation (MDL 3094) alleging failure to warn about gastrointestinal and visual risks.
ABPI / PMCPA (UK): Suspended for 2 years over a disguised marketing campaign for Saxenda, later reinstated in March 2025 following compliance audits.
U.S. DOJ: Paid $6.3 million to resolve False Claims Act allegations concerning Trade Agreements Act violations for pen needles manufactured in non-designated countries.
U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey: Settled securities class action for $100 million regarding financial disclosures on U.S. insulin price pressures without admission of liability.
Copenhagen City Court: International institutional investors' DKK 1.8 billion lawsuit over sales forecasts and U.S. pricing pressures resolved with zero payment.
U.S. DOJ / FDA: Agreed to pay $58.65 million and entered a Corporate Integrity Agreement over Victoza REMS and off-label promotion allegations.
U.S. DOJ: Paid $25 million to resolve civil liability regarding off-label promotion of NovoSeven.
